title: Does worst-case Nearest Codeword hardness imply low-noise LPN hardness?
formal: Does the following implication hold? If binary Nearest Codeword is not in BPP, then no uniform probabilistic polynomial-time distinguisher D has advantage at least $n^{-c}$, for any fixed $c>0$ and all sufficiently large square n, between $(A,As+e)$ and $(A,u)$. Here $A\in\mathbb F_2^{n^2\times n}$, $s\in\mathbb F_2^n$, and $u\in\mathbb F_2^{n^2}$ are independent uniform random variables, and the coordinates of e are independent Bernoulli variables with rate $1/\sqrt n$. Advantage is the absolute difference of D’s acceptance probabilities in the two experiments.
context:
LWE has strong connections to worst-case lattice problems. Establishing comparable foundations for LPN at cryptographically useful noise rates is more difficult.

Without noise, enough independent parity equations reveal the secret by linear algebra. Flipping some answers breaks that direct procedure: the learner must cope with equations whose right-hand sides may be wrong. At a low noise rate, most equations remain correct, which makes the precise source of hardness especially important.

A worst-case-to-average-case reduction would start with an arbitrary hard coding instance and turn it into the random samples used by LPN. It must preserve a usable noise regime and show how an LPN solver would solve the original task. Requiring two different coding tasks to be hard simultaneously is a stronger premise than deriving the guarantee from one standard worst-case problem.
why: A basic security assumption would obtain an explanation through independently studied hardness. The extra assumption in the new reduction makes the remaining target concrete.

progress.text: The revision gives a reduction for $\eta=n^{-\alpha}$, any constant $\alpha<1$, from simultaneous worst-case hardness of two tasks on a code and its dual. This advances beyond earlier near-half-noise reductions; the single-assumption target remains stronger.

references.title: Towards Worst-case Hardness for Low-Noise LPN
references.authors: Divesh Aggarwal; Rishav Gupta; Hai Hoang Nguyen; Kel Zin Tan; Prashant Nalini Vasudevan

status_note: Literature checked on 10 September 2026; dates and review scope are recorded below.
review_note: Editorial specialization of the NCP-only direction in Section 1.2 of the September 2026 revision. It fixes the starting problem, decision-LPN distribution, sample count, noise, uniformity, and asymptotic advantage, replacing the vague phrase natural worst-case problem. The source does not state this exact parameter specialization as a numbered conjecture.

definitions: Binary Nearest Codeword receives a binary matrix G, a binary target y with the same number of rows, and an integer t, and asks whether $\min_z\operatorname{wt}(Gz-y)\le t$, with arithmetic over F_2 and Hamming weight wt. BPP means a uniform randomized polynomial-time decider correct with probability at least 2/3 on every instance. The LPN side here is a decision problem with n-squared samples, random secret, and inverse-square-root noise. Restricting n to squares makes the noise parameter an exact rational; this is an explicit specialization of the source’s broader low-noise direction.
answer_criterion: Prove the displayed complexity-theoretic implication, for example by a reduction turning such an LPN distinguisher into a BPP algorithm for Nearest Codeword, or prove that the implication is false. Invoking simultaneous hardness of an additional problem on the dual code does not establish this implication.

importance.reason: Would connect worst-case coding hardness to a central average-case cryptographic assumption in a concrete low-noise regime.
